src/domain/product.ts createProduct: `if (!id.trim()) throw new DomainError("Product id is required");`
src/domain/product.ts declares `interface Product { id; name; stock }` and `interface CatalogueProduct { id; name; stock }` with the same shape

parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files belong to the same order/catalogue domain, but the module repeats rules and abstractions that should each live in one place. (1) The rule that a product id is required is written twice: once in product.ts createProduct and again in order.ts createOrder, each with its own copy of the message "Product id is required". (2) product.ts declares two interfaces with the same shape, Product and CatalogueProduct, so there are two competing abstractions for one concept. (3) The rule for a required id is applied differently: createOrder checks `!id`, so an id made only of spaces passes, while createProduct checks `!id.trim()`. (4) DomainError is the shared error type for the whole module, but it is declared in product.ts. That makes order.ts depend on the product file just to get the error type, which blurs the boundary between the two files. Points 1 and 2 match the rubric's fail conditions.
